doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

chapter: Photographs of the Creole Fiesta and family
title: Family photographs in the patio
summary: Edna names relatives in a patio photo and a Christmas tree she grew.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Now, this is my family. My family taking in the patio. You can see with all the leaves how my garden has gone. This is, um, my sister. She lives in Buffalo, New York. Mrs. Causey. Mrs. Susan B. Causey. This is my brother, Clarence Bibelet. Clarence Bibelet. He lives up on Cater Street. This is me, Edna Bibelet. This is my husband, Franz Calvin Bibelet. And this is the children. This is Edwin, Newmire. You heard of the, um, the school, the Martinez Children's School? Oh, Martinez.

Martinez, yes, yes. This is her son. She's my cousin. This is her son. And this is the one who drives. Louise Bibelet. That's my nephew. And this is Anne Marie. She was the maid this year. From that time, look how she's grown. She was maid this year. That's Anne Marie, Anne Marie Serena. This is Sylvia. And this is my grandson. He's in, he's in, um, in the Air Force Station at San Francisco. Now, this is, um, Iris May. You could help if you come to me. Iris May. Turn around this way. Iris May. I had so many to think of. And this is Mildred Martinez. She is the, she's the owner of that school. And this is, uh, Louise Bibelet. My, my nephew, niece-in-law. That's my nephew's wife. And her little girl, Brenda. And my daughter-in-law, uh, Alfreda Serena. Alfreda Serena. And she's the owner of the family. So that's the family. I haven't seen the Christmas tree.
You didn't have it? Oh, that's right there. That's a huge Christmas tree.

I grew, I grew this Christmas tree. That was the next door. Next door, I grew this Christmas tree. You see the part of the house? So, it was so pretty that year. I told my husband, I said, let's dress up and take a picture. So I got a photographer and took this picture. And good thing the next year died. You know what happened? That was, that was history. Everybody would stop their cause. So look at that tree. It was so pretty.
It looks like poinsettias and boom right around. Well, that's right.
That's right. Whatever. So, thank you.
